articles.title: Nvidia leadership crisis, higher oil prices and yields, weighed on equities
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
After admitting earlier this week that he had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, Jensen Huang 
resigned
 as CEO of Nvidia yesterday. This, along with higher Brent oil prices and interest rates, negatively impacted risk appetite with stock market declines in the US (S&P 500 -0.4%, Nasdaq -0.4%) although European stocks advanced (Euro Stoxx 50 +0.1%). The euro weakened against the dollar while the price of gold fell. In Asia, stock markets are opening upwards in Japan, down in China. 
Geopolitics
. President Trump said the U.S. 
doesn't need a deal
 with Iran and called on Vice President J.D. Vance to focus on corruption in opposition-controlled electoral districts. The president also threatened to 
double tariffs on Mexico
 if the country's government doesn't stop a group of about 1,500 migrants from walking toward the U.S. border. Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the President of Ukraine, stated that Starshield service has once again 
been limited
 for the country's armed forces and therefore makes its drone defense difficult. 
Statistics.
 Today, October's final inflation data for France, Spain and Poland will be released. In addition, the second estimate of euro area GDP and employment for the third quarter will be published. In the US, producer price inflation for October will be published, in Russia inflation and in Turkey, September's current account will be released. Today's only interest rate announcement comes from Peru, where a 25 basis point hike is expected.
Speeches related to central banks are expected from the Fed's Mary Daly, Michelle Bowman, Susan Collins, and from the ECB's Isabel Schnabel, Ante Žigman and Olaf Sleijpen. Updated credit ratings are expected for Bulgaria (S&P), Germany (Fitch) and Ukraine (Moody's).

Nordic key stories
The krona weakened yesterday and the OMX30 index ended unchanged.
Center Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist has requested concrete government proposals from both the Moderate Party's Ulf Kristersson and the Social Democrats' Magdalena Andersson, and the proposals must be submitted no later than today at 5 p.m. 
The General Council of the Riksbank will meet at 1 p.m.

articles.title: Uneasy calm
articles.heading: SEB FI & FX Strategy
articles.fulltext:
At a glance:
 In market focus. AI; France; Middle East.
Global macro and risk appetite.
 The rotation out of tech/AI reflects concerns over datacentre investment, initially driven by rising funding and input costs rather than fears of political restrictions, particularly at state level, following the Democratic midterm sweep. We see no major hit to investment plans as rates have fallen, and moratorium calls appear aimed at making builders bear more water and energy costs, not blocking construction. We expect AI capex growth to slow more than consensus anticipates in 2027, without turning negative, levelling off in 2028, and expect Anthropic’s IPO to be successful. The greater threat is AI revenues as fading confidence in future profits would undermine the investment case. Cheaper oil, lower rates and lower chip prices would support the non-tech economy. Our base case is that tech stocks bottom out around current levels, allowing the broader market to rebound.
US macro: Robust labour market, sticky inflation. 
Recent data (payrolls, CPI) highlight the continued strong economic momentum coupled with increased risks for indirect effects from a prolonged period of elevated price pressures from tariffs, energy and the AI buildout. Modest wage growth together with productivity growth at or above 2% means that the labour market is not an inflation problem and that current inflation pressures are temporary. We continue to expect that inflation will be back at the target by the end of 2028, but short-term upside risks have increased.
USD short rates: Policy is still expansionary. 
Continued upside growth surprises suggest that current policy is not restrictive and support that the Fed has more to do. While Fed Governor Waller has raised the possibility of a larger 50bp step in December, we think the Fed majority still leans towards smaller and gradual steps, of 25bp at every second meeting. We expect the Fed to deliver a 25bp hike in December, possibly followed by another 25bp increase at the March meeting. Further equity market turbulence and a faster decline in energy prices pose downside risks to the aggressive tightening path currently priced in by markets.
USD bonds: Abrupt end to the bond rally.
 Higher-than-expected October CPI and hawkish comments from Fed Governor Waller pushed yields higher after an extended bond rally since early October. Forwards now price in around 80bp of hikes by next autumn, which we see as broadly fair given the balance of risks. We expect the 10Y Treasury yield to trade near 5% in the coming weeks.
France: Brace for renewed turbulence.
 A key milestone is midnight on 17 December, when the 70-day constitutional period for Parliament to reach a decision on the 2027 budget bill reportedly expires. If Parliament has neither definitively adopted nor definitively rejected the bill, Article 47 permits, but does not oblige, the government to bring its provisions into force by ordinance, without parliamentary adoption. Article 49.3 provides a separate route to adoption without a vote in the National Assembly, provided no resulting no-confidence motion succeeds.
Eurosystem: Cracks in the plumbing? 
The Q3 quarter-end spike in EUR repo rates highlights the importance of how cash moves through the banking system as the ECB’s balance sheet shrinks. While repo-market volatility can signal emerging pressures, we interpret the spike primarily as a consequence of quarter-end intermediation constraints rather than evidence of a system-wide liquidity shortage.
EUR short rates: Next hike in December. 
Several Governing Council members have recently signalled a need for a December hike, stressed that France must address its fiscal issues and downplayed the implications of the fiscal turbulence for monetary policy. Forwards price in around 70bp of hikes by autumn 2027. In our view, pricing in 50-55bp of hikes in total would be fair at this stage.
EUR bonds: Reasonable rebound.
 Sovereign spreads have narrowed from their recent peaks but remain vulnerable to France-related turbulence in the months ahead. Optimism over a Middle East resolution and softer ECB rate expectations briefly pushed the 10Y Bund yield below our Q4 target range of 3.30-3.50% before it rebounded. A sustained decline in yields looks unlikely until the policy-rate peak draws closer.
EUR/USD:
Bulls and bears lurk in the shadows.
EUR/USD should remain broadly range-bound in the near term. Relative rates and resilient US growth still support the dollar, but much of the adjustment has already occurred and positioning is stretched short EUR. Europe’s winter energy risk also looks increasingly contained. However, larger moves remain possible in both directions. A Hormuz agreement combined with an AI/US led equity sell-off could drive EUR/USD higher, while renewed escalation around Hormuz alongside increased fiscal and political stress in France would reinforce the downside.
Forecasts.
 Links to SEB’s official 
macro
, 
central bank
 and 
financial
 forecasts. 
Eurosystem: Quarter-end strains, not yet evidence of a broader liquidity shortage
The sharp rise in EUR repo rates at the end of September was a reminder that ample liquidity across the banking system does not prevent temporary increases in money market rates relative to the policy rates. We interpret the repo spike primarily as a consequence of quarter-end constraints on banks’ willingness and capacity to intermediate cash, rather than evidence of a system-wide liquidity shortage. Overnight repo rates largely retreated after quarter-end. Even so, the episode highlights an issue worth monitoring: as the Eurosystem reduces its balance sheet, the cost of redistributing cash through the banking system is becoming more volatile.
What happened?
 Repo markets allow banks and other financial institutions to borrow cash against securities. They are a key source of short-term funding and an important channel for moving liquidity between market participants.
On 30 September, CME’s RFR Euro general-collateral (GC) one-day repo rate rose to 2.72%, around 16bp above preceding levels. Another measure of secured funding costs, the STOXX GC Pooling overnight rate, reached 2.63%, up approximately 12bp from the previous day. French and Italian one-day RFR repo rates rose more than German rates and retained a larger premium in subsequent sessions (chart below). 
Big-4 one-day RFR repos (GC & SC) vs. €STR (bp)
Source: ECB, CME, Bloomberg, SEB. Note: RFR repo is a composite rate that includes both general collateral and specific collateral one-day repo transactions.
A brief spike around a reporting date does not, by itself, establish that money markets are malfunctioning or that an ECB response is needed. What matters is whether elevated spreads persist beyond quarter-end and whether money market rate volatility becomes excessive.
Why ample liquidity did not prevent the spike.
 Excess liquidity in the Eurosystem remains around EUR 2.1tn. But this aggregate figure does not show where reserves are held or how readily they are available. Some banks hold substantially more reserves than others, while payment needs and desired liquidity buffers also differ. Individual borrowers can therefore face tighter funding conditions even when the system as a whole has ample reserves. 
Eurosystem balance sheet: Assets (EUR bn)
Closing those gaps requires institutions with available liquidity to lend, either directly or through intermediaries. Having cash, however, is not the same as being willing or able to deploy it. Regulatory requirements, internal counterparty limits and banks’ own balance-sheet priorities can constrain lending. Borrowing cash to lend it on can also tie up additional balance-sheet capacity.
These constraints can become more binding around quarter-end, when banks manage their balance sheets for reporting purposes. The resulting reduction in intermediation can restrict the supply of cash just as reporting-date demand increases, pushing repo rates higher without implying an aggregate shortage of reserves. This is our main interpretation of September’s episode.
Why this matters as liquidity declines.
 The Eurosystem’s balance-sheet reduction is gradually changing the backdrop. As bonds held under its asset-purchase programmes (APP and PEPP) mature without reinvestment, excess liquidity declines, other things equal. Banks consequently become more reliant on money markets to obtain the liquidity they need to settle payments. Obstacles to moving cash through the system then become more consequential.
Repo-market volatility can therefore provide an early warning of pressure as liquidity becomes less abundant. The distinction is between temporary reporting-date strains and more persistent funding difficulties. We are watching three indicators:
Whether funding pressures persist beyond quarter-end.
Whether differences in funding conditions across countries persist.
Whether banks increase their use of Eurosystem refinancing operations.
Persistent pressures alongside broader financing difficulties would challenge the view that September’s spike was mainly a temporary intermediation issue.
ECB unlikely to intervene in the near term. 
Temporary repo-rate spikes are unlikely to prompt an early ECB response. Since announcing its revised operational framework in March 2024, the ECB has reiterated that it will introduce structural longer-term refinancing operations and begin building a structural securities portfolio only once the Eurosystem’s balance sheet starts to grow sustainably.
The ECB is currently reviewing the framework and we expect the findings to be published in H1 2027, potentially as early as Q1. Our baseline is for structural refinancing operations to be introduced in late 2027, followed by a structural securities portfolio in 2028.
For more on our expected timeline, see
 SEB FI & FX Strategy: Transition to a demand-driven Eurosystem
, 30 October.
What this means for swap spreads. 
We expect the €STR/6M Euribor basis to remain an important driver of German government bond spreads against 6M Euribor swaps in the coming months. At the height of the French market turbulence, German government bond yields fell significantly below corresponding Euribor swap rates. That gap has narrowed more recently as French sovereign spreads have retreated from their recent highs. 
German government - Euribor 6M swaps (MM spread, bp)
Source: Bloomberg, SEB.
Renewed France-related volatility would likely widen the €STR/6M Euribor basis, widening the gap between German government yields and 6M Euribor swap rates, other things equal. In that case, German government bonds may also likely richen against €STR swaps as investors seek safety, reinforcing their richening against Euribor swaps. 
STR/Euribor 6M basis (bp)
Over the longer term, however, we expect declining excess liquidity to push repo rates higher relative to €STR, supporting a cheapening of German government bonds against €STR swaps. A narrower €STR/6M Euribor basis once liquidity conditions stabilise later in 2027 and in 2028 would reinforce their cheapening against 6M Euribor swaps, consistent with the longer-term targets shown in the chart above.
EUR/USD: Bulls and bears lurk in the shadows
We expect EUR/USD to trade broadly sideways from here. Relative rates still favour the dollar and resilient US growth provides support, but EUR/USD has already adjusted significantly to the change in the rates backdrop. Positioning is also stretched short EUR, which should slow further downside unless there is a more structural break.
The recent dollar strength is understandable. US data remain solid, inflation has surprised to the upside and the market has repriced the Fed higher. Longer US yields have risen alongside the dollar, while the US-euro 2Y differential has again moved in favour of the USD. However, the rate driven move start to look priced. With around 80bp of Fed hikes priced by next autumn, broadly in line with our assessment of the risks, another material rise in the dollar increasingly requires further hawkish repricing rather than confirmation of the existing story.
At the same time, one of the euro’s main downside risks is becoming less threatening. Europe increasingly looks capable of navigating even a hard winter without returning to acute energy stress. Inventories remain stable, reducing the need for a large winter energy risk premium in the euro. Energy therefore looks less likely to provide the catalyst for a structural move lower in EUR/USD.
This suggests that the latest move is more likely part of a broader range than the start of a sustained trend lower. Further downside remains possible if US data continue to surprise on the upside, but a lasting break would probably require a larger theme. Further out, the balance of risks is less clear, with credible drivers for larger moves in both directions. 
The risk for a larger upside scenario for EUR/USD is mainly a dollar story. USD positioning is long, leaving the currency vulnerable if the US exceptionalism narrative weakens. An AI-driven correction in US equities could increasingly resemble a “sell USA” episode rather than a conventional dollar-positive risk-off shock, particularly given the large unhedged foreign equity inflows into the US. 
The downside risk case is mainly a euro story. France is at risk of becoming an increasingly important EUR risk through 2027. French fiscal dynamics remain difficult even under relatively benign assumptions for growth and refinancing costs, while a large share of government debt must be refinanced over the coming five years. Renewed political instability or wider French sovereign spreads could therefore weigh on the euro. It could also restrict the ECB’s ability to raise rates as higher funding costs are already tightening French financial conditions.
Bottomline:
 EUR/USD has room to recover moderately near term if energy risk premium fades, with renewed pressure from French fiscal and political risks pushed further into 2027. Faster energy disinflation and a broader global recovery would weigh on the dollar. Escalation in Hormuz and renewed French stress would drive EUR/USD lower. A larger move higher would likely require a Hormuz deal combined with a US equity sell-off, while a larger move lower would likely require renewed escalation in Hormuz alongside increased stress in France.

articles.heading: Swedish inflation
articles.fulltext:
CPIF ex energy was significantly lower than expected a for a third month in a row. A weaker exchange rate and indirect effects from energy suggest that core inflation will rise over the next 12 months but PPI on consumer goods and pricing plans in the NIER survey are still muted. The near-term forecast for core inflation has been lowered. Energy prices continue to be volatile and fuel prices seem set to decline by around 10% in November. Electricity prices will rise sharply in November but futures in the beginning of next year have declined.

articles.title: Confirming a cyclical peak
articles.heading: Norwegian Oil Investment Survey
articles.fulltext:
The Q4 petroleum investment survey shows that operators have revised their nominal investment estimate for 2026 downwards to NOK 266bn. While still historically high, this implies a 2.7% decline from actual spending in 2025. The estimate for 2027 was revised higher but remains 10.4% below the corresponding estimate for 2026. With major developments projects nearing completion and the pipeline thinning, the survey reinforces our view that the petroleum investment cycle is shifting. The (nominal) decline indicated in 2026 and 2027 are broadly consistent with Norges Bank’s assumption in its Sep MPR. 
Investment cycle: 
Petroleum investment has reached record-high levels following the pandemic-era tax package, but the cycle is now maturing. Several projects sanctioned under the package were completed in 2025 or earlier in 2026, contributing to lower estimates for field development this year. However, the largest projects remain under construction and are expected to be finished in 2027. The petroleum sector will thus lend negative demand impulses to mainland GDP from next year.
Investment outlook 2026:
 Operators have revised their nominal investment estimates for 2026 downward by NOK 9bn to 266bn, implying a 2.7% decline relative to actual spending in 2025. The downward revision in the Q4 survey is primarily driven by field development and fields on stream. Compared to the corresponding survey given a year ago (i.e. 2025 Q4 survey), aggregate investments are 3.4% lower and the decline is broad-based; exploration is significantly lower (-21.4%), while the largest sub-categories fields on stream and field development are slightly lower at -3.0% and -3.1%, respectively. 
Investment outlook 2027:
 The Q4 survey shows another upward revision to nominal investments by NOK 9bn to 237bn in 2027. Nonetheless, this is 10.9% lower than the current estimate for 2026 and 4.8% lower compared to the corresponding estimate for 2026 given a year ago (i.e. Q4 survey in 2025). This is driven by a 15.4% decline in field developments although an 8.0% increase in fields on stream dampens the overall fall. Despite the decline, the estimate for field developments was lifted by NOK 10.6bn compared to the previous survey. This mostly reflects higher reported costs, e.g. measures to ensure that the planned start-up time for production is realized and currency effects, and will thus not lift investment activity measured in volume terms. 
Implications for Norges Bank:
 In its Sep MPR, Norges Bank projected a 3.5% decline in petroleum investments (previously 3.0%). While it still expects a sizeable decline in 2027, it revised its forecast up by 1.0ppt to -4.0%. The survey confirms the notion of a cyclical peak, which is further underpinned by higher expected costs related to shutdown and removal. As some additional developments projects have entered the pipeline after summer, this will lift investments somewhat, though not enough to offset the fall in investments.

articles.title: Record stock market in Stockholm and a budget without reforms
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Risk appetite returned yesterday after CoreWeave’s report eased concerns about AI investment following this week’s slump in Nvidia. Nasdaq rose 1.6% and the S&P 500 gained 1.3%. Futures, however, point to a lower open today. The Stockholm stock exchange rose for a third straight day, up 1.0% yesterday to a new record high. It is now up 17% since the start of the year, 7 percentage points more than in an average year. Oil rose to around USD 95 per barrel yesterday before falling back overnight, and gold, which now trades more like a risk asset, fell below USD 4,000 per ounce.
The AI pendulum swung back.
 CoreWeave, which rents out computing power for AI, raised its full-year guidance and expects to reach adjusted profitability in the first half of 2028, easing concerns about the company’s debt. At the same time, Anthropic is reported to be considering a higher valuation for its IPO after record demand. This also calmed a volatile market that has become an important macro issue because of its financial and economic impact.
Prisoner swap but no breakthrough in Abu Dhabi.
 Two days of talks have brought no breakthrough on the big issues of territory, security guarantees and a ceasefire. The parties did agree in principle on a larger prisoner exchange, whose scope is to be finalised today. The ball is now in Moscow’s court, where US envoys Witkoff and Kushner travel today to meet Putin.
Strong UK GDP expected for the third quarter.
 Consensus expects 0.7% q/q, which would show that the economy has so far weathered the energy shock and that underlying growth is stronger than expected. A significant part of this year’s growth is estimated to come from AI, but mainly from building and developing the technology rather than from its spread through the economy. Whether it brings broader effects remains to be seen. A strong outcome would be in line with our relatively optimistic forecast of 1.4% for 2026. That is needed to ease pressure on public finances ahead of 2027, a much tougher year in which the economy turns down and major budget issues must be settled.
General strike in Spain ahead of the snap election.
 According to the unions, millions of workers walked out yesterday in the country’s first general strike in 14 years, with the housing crisis as the main issue. The same issue triggered the snap election on 29 November. The Socialists trail in the polls, and the People’s Party together with the right-wing populist Vox could win a majority of their own. The economy is strong, however, and we do not expect the election to affect growth significantly.
Norwegian oil investment at 08:00.
 In the previous survey, plans for 2027 were lifted sharply to NOK 227bn, mainly after three new development plans were submitted, but the level is still just over 17% below this year’s. The peak appears to have passed, and investment is expected to decline next year as few new projects are in the pipeline.
Nordic key stories
Neutral caretaker budget presented today.
 Finance Minister Elisabeth Svantesson presents a budget for 2027 that mainly extends earlier decisions without new reforms. The exception is necessary adjustments to maintain key public functions, such as defence and the prison service. Other initiatives are put on hold, including a planned SEK 1.5bn boost to research and the expansion of higher vocational education. The more interesting budget debate follows at 13:00, where the contours of a government majority may begin to emerge. The other parties have until 27 November to submit counter-proposals, and the Tidö parties have not ruled out a budget of their own.
Global rates pull Swedish rates higher.
 The Swedish 2-year yield has risen 14bp over the past two days, driven mainly by the repricing towards a hawkish Fed but also by the Riksbank minutes. The scope for a further rise should be limited, however, as the Riksbank’s position looks better, but the move shows how both domestic and global forces drive rates. Today, First Deputy Governor Aino Bunge speaks on the economic situation and monetary policy at 13:15. It is the first chance to hear whether the hawkish tone of the minutes holds, or whether the low inflation outcome for October weighs more heavily. We also expect today’s final inflation figures to confirm the picture from the flash estimate.

articles.title: Rekordbörs i Stockholm och en budget utan reformer
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Riskaptiten återvände i går efter att CoreWeaves rapport dämpat oron för AI-investeringarna efter veckans ras i Nvidia, och Nasdaq steg 1,6 % medan S&P 500 gick upp 1,3 %. Terminerna pekar dock mot en röd öppning i dag. Stockholmsbörsen steg för tredje dagen i rad, i går med 1,0 % till ny rekordnivå. Sedan årsskiftet är börsen nu upp 17 %, vilket är 7 procentenheter mer än ett genomsnittligt år. Oljan steg till runt 95 dollar per fat under gårdagen innan det föll tillbaka under natten, vilket fick guldet som nu handlas mer som en riskfylld tillgång att falla under 4 000 dollar per uns.
AI-pendeln svängde tillbaka
. CoreWeave, som hyr ut datorkraft för AI, höjde helårsprognosen och räknar med justerad lönsamhet under första halvåret 2028, vilket dämpade oron för bolagets skulder. Samtidigt rapporteras att Anthropic överväger en högre värdering inför sin börsnotering efter rekordstort intresse, något som också lugnade den volatila marknaden som nu blivit en viktig makrofråga till följd av dess finansiella och ekonomiska påverkan. 
Fångutväxling men inget genombrott i Abu Dhabi.
 Efter två dagars samtal finns inget genombrott i de stora frågorna om territorium, säkerhetsgarantier och vapenvila. Parterna enades dock i princip om en större fångutväxling, vars omfattning ska spikas under dagen. Nu ligger bollen hos Moskva, dit de amerikanska sändebuden Witkoff och Kushner reser i dag för att träffa Putin.
Stark brittisk BNP väntas för tredje kvartalet.
 Konsensus väntar sig 0,7 % i kvartalstakt, vilket skulle visa att ekonomin hittills klarat energichocken och att den underliggande tillväxten är starkare än väntat. En betydande del av årets tillväxt beräknas komma från AI, men främst från att tekniken byggs och utvecklas snarare än från att den sprids i ekonomin. Om det ger bredare effekter återstår att se. Ett starkt utfall skulle ligga i linje med vår relativt optimistiska prognos på 1,4 % för 2026. Det behövs för att minska pressen på statsfinanserna inför 2027, ett betydligt svårare år då ekonomin vänder ned och stora budgetfrågor ska avgöras.
Generalstrejk i Spanien inför nyvalet.
 Enligt facken lade miljontals arbetare ned arbetet i går i landets första generalstrejk på 14 år, med bostadskrisen som huvudfråga. Det var samma fråga som utlöste nyvalet den 29 november. Socialisterna ligger efter i mätningarna, och Folkpartiet kan tillsammans med högerpopulistiska Vox nå egen majoritet. Ekonomin går dock starkt, och vi väntar oss inte att valet påverkar tillväxten nämnvärt.
Norska oljeinvesteringar kl. 08.00.
 I förra undersökningen lyftes planerna för 2027 kraftigt till 227 miljarder kronor, främst efter att tre nya utbyggnadsplaner lämnats in, men nivån ligger ändå drygt 17 % under årets. Toppen verkar vara passerad, och investeringarna väntas minska nästa år när få nya projekt står på tur.
Sverige
Neutral övergångsbudget läggs fram i dag. 
Finansminister Elisabeth Svantesson presenterar en budget för 2027 som i huvudsak förlänger tidigare beslut utan nya reformer. Undantaget är nödvändiga justeringar för att upprätthålla viktiga samhällsfunktioner, till exempel försvaret och kriminalvården. Andra satsningar läggs på is, bland annat ett planerat tillskott på 1,5 miljarder till forskningen och utbyggnaden av yrkeshögskolan. Den mer intressanta budgetdebatten följer kl. 13.00 där konturerna av ett regeringsunderlag eventuellt börjar ses. Övriga partier har till den 27 november på sig att lägga motförslag, och Tidöpartierna har inte uteslutit en egen budget.
Globala räntor drar med sig de svenska. 
Den svenska 2-årsräntan har stigit 14 punkter de senaste två dagarna, främst driven av omprisningen mot ett hökaktigt Fed men även av Riksbanksprotokollet. Utrymmet för en fortsatt uppgång bör dock vara begränsat, eftersom Riksbankens förutsättningar ser bättre ut, men rörelsen visar hur både inhemska och globala krafter påverkar räntorna. Idag talar förste vice riksbankschef Aino Bunge om det ekonomiska läget och penningpolitiken kl. 13.15 vilket blir första chansen att höra om protokollets hökaktiga ton står sig, eller om det låga inflationsutfallet för oktober väger tyngre. Vi väntar oss även att dagens slutliga inflationssiffror bekräftar bilden från flashen.

articles.title: Sticky inflation keeps the Fed on a hiking path
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
US rates set the tone yesterday after hawkish comments and a CPI print above consensus. The US 2-year yield rose by around 20bp, and the market is now fully pricing a 25bp hike in December, with a 15% probability of a double hike. The S&P 500 fell 0.4% and Nasdaq 0.7%, while Nvidia dropped a further 5.5%. European equities closed higher, with the Eurostoxx 50 up 0.6% and the OMXS30 up 0.5%. Oil prices have been weighed down by hopes that the war with Iran is drawing to a close, but new attacks on ships are keeping part of the risk premium in place, and Brent is trading around USD 92 per barrel. Asia is mixed, with the Nikkei heading for a third day of gains while Hong Kong is lower.  
Third straight month of surprisingly high US core inflation.
 The surprise was small but broad: services, rents and goods all rose more than the market had expected. Core inflation came in at 2.8% y/y, and the annualised rate over the past three months was close to 4%, a trend pointing slightly up rather than down. Together with Waller’s hawkish comment about a double hike and Friday’s strong jobs report, this strengthens our forecast of a hike in December.
Abu Dhabi peace talks enter their second day.
 The US, Ukraine and Russia met yesterday in Abu Dhabi for their first peace talks since February. The US side described the first day as “very productive”. However, the parties remain far apart on territory and security guarantees, and expectations of a breakthrough are low.
Norwegian core inflation in line with Norges Bank.
 CPI-ATE fell to 2.7% in October, one tenth below our forecast. Lower food prices and cheaper imported goods both contributed, which may be a sign that the stronger krone has started to feed through to prices. Higher rents in October are an upside risk, as they carry a large weight in the CPI basket. Overall, the inflation picture supports our view that inflation will come in lower than Norges Bank expects.
In today’s 
Ögat
, we sum up the key conclusions from our recently published Nordic Outlook.
 We also look at the US midterm elections, where the Democrats’ unexpectedly strong gains are putting pressure not only on Trump and the Republicans but also on oil prices and AI investment.
Nordic key stories
More hawkish minutes than expected.
 The minutes from last week’s rate hike painted a tighter picture than both the press release and the press conference. Per Jansson and Göran Hjelm in particular highlighted upside risks to inflation from energy prices and stronger growth. Jansson and Anna Seim both left the door open to a hike as early as December, while Governor Erik Thedéen expects hikes in line with the September path, i.e. roughly over the coming six months. However, the low October inflation print, a stronger krona and lower energy prices suggest there is no rush. We stick to our view that the rate will be left unchanged in December and raised one last time in March.
Mixed Swedish data.
 Yesterday’s production figures showed private-sector output falling 0.5% in September, which was expected after several consecutive months of gains. We remain positive on Swedish growth and expect GDP to grow by 3.0% this year, but 2027 will bring headwinds from more expensive energy, rising mortgage rates and the phase-out of support measures, which is likely to dampen consumption. Household consumption data at 08:00 today will give further signals on the state of the Swedish economy.
Kristersson given until 17 November.
 The Speaker has extended the exploratory mandate, and Kristersson will now present a basis for a government next Tuesday. Everything hinges on whether he can present a credible plan to bring the Centre Party on board. Without a new government in place tomorrow, the caretaker government will present a budget that, by convention, should be neutral and pared back.

articles.title: Envis inflation håller Fed på höjarspåret
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Den amerikanska räntemarknaden satte tonen under gårdagen efter hökaktiga uttalanden och en KPI-siffra över konsensus. Den amerikanska 2-årsräntan steg med runt 20 baspunkter, och marknaden prisar nu fullt ut en höjning med 25 baspunkter i december, med 15 % sannolikhet för en dubbelhöjning. S&P 500 backade med 0,4 % och Nasdaq med 0,7 %, och Nvidia föll ytterligare 5,5 %, medan europeiska börser stängde på plus med Eurostoxx 50 på + 0,6 % och OMXS30 på + 0,5 %. Oljepriset har pressats av förhoppningarna om att kriget med Iran går mot sitt slut, men nya attacker mot fartyg håller kvar en del av riskpremien, och Brent handlas runt 92 dollar per fat. I Asien är bilden blandad, där Nikkei går mot en tredje dag med uppgång medan Hongkongbörsen backar.
Tredje månaden i rad med oväntat hög kärninflation i USA. 
Överraskningen var liten men bred: tjänster, hyror och varor steg alla mer än marknaden hade räknat med. Kärninflationen landade på 2,8 % i årstakt och den uppräknade årstakten för de senaste tre månaderna låg nära 4 %, en trend som pekar svagt uppåt i stället för nedåt. I kombination med Wallers hökaktiga uttalande om en dubbelhöjning samt fredagens starka jobbrapport stärks vår prognos om en höjning i december.
Fredssamtalen i Abu Dhabi går in på sin andra dag. 
USA, Ukraina och Ryssland möttes igår för första gången sedan februari för fredssamtal i Abu Dhabi. Från amerikansk sida ansågs den första dagens samtal ha varit ”väldigt produktiva”. Dock står parterna fortfarande långt ifrån varandra i frågor gällande territorium och säkerhetsgarantier, och förväntningarna på ett genombrott är låga.
Norsk kärninflation i linje med Norges Bank. 
KPI-JAE sjönk till 2,7 % i oktober, en tiondel under vår prognos. Både lägre priser på livsmedel och importerade varor bidrog, vilket kan vara tecken på att den starkare kronan börjat påverka priserna. Högre hyror i oktober är en uppsidesrisk då de väger tungt i KPI-korgen. Den övergripande bilden är att inflationsutvecklingen stödjer vår bedömning att inflationen blir lägre än vad Norges Bank räknar med. 
I dagen
s 
Ögat 
sam
manfattar vi de viktigaste slutsatserna
 från vår nyligen publicerade Nordic Outlook. Vi summerar också mellanårsvalet i USA, där de oväntat stora demokratiska framgångarna inte bara pressar Trump och Republikanerna utan även oljepriset och AI-investeringarna. 
Sverige
Hökaktigare protokoll än väntat. 
Protokollet från förra veckans räntehöjning gav en stramare bild än både pressmeddelandet och presskonferensen. Framför allt Per Jansson och Göran Hjelm lyfte uppsidesrisker för inflationen från energipriser och starkare tillväxt. Jansson och Anna Seim höll båda dörren öppen för en höjning redan i december, medan riksbankschef Erik Thedéen räknar med höjningar i linje med septemberbanan, alltså ungefär under det kommande halvåret. Det låga inflationsutfallet för oktober, en starkare krona och lägre energipriser talar dock för att det inte är bråttom. Vi står fast vid att räntan lämnas oförändrad i december och höjs en sista gång i mars. 
Blandad svensk statistik. 
Gårdagens produktionssiffror visade att produktionen i den privata sektorn backade med 0,5 % i september, vilket var väntat efter flera månader i rad med uppgång. Vi är fortsatt positiva till svensk tillväxt och räknar med att BNP växer med 3,0 % i år men att 2027 för med sig motvind i form av dyrare energi, stigande bolåneräntor och avvecklade stöd, vilket lär dämpa konsumtionen. Vid 08:00 idag kommer statistik kring hushållens konsumtion som ger ytterligare signaler om tillståndet i svensk ekonomi. 
Kristersson får tid till den 17 november.
 Talmannen har förlängt sonderingsuppdraget, och Kristersson ska nu redovisa ett regeringsunderlag nästa tisdag. Allt hänger på om han kan presentera en trovärdig plan för att få med Centerpartiet. Utan en ny regering på plats i morgon lägger övergångsregeringen fram en budget som enligt praxis ska vara neutral och avskalad.

articles.title: Tillväxten utmanas av höga räntor och energipriser
articles.heading: Ögat
articles.fulltext:
I vår nyligen publicerade Nordic Outlook Update konstaterar vi att global BNP växer med drygt 3 procent per år, trots global osäkerhet, obalanser på energimarknaden och stigande räntor. Inflationsoro får ECB och Fed att höja räntan ytterligare en eller två gånger. Vi höjer svenska BNP-prognosen för i år, men ser motvindar från energi och räntor nästa år. Riksbanken höjer styrräntan i mars, till 2,25 procent och ligger kvar på den nivån under 2028. 
Mellanårsvalet i USA: Blå våg pressar oljepriset och AI
Demokraterna tog som väntat över kongressen. Det tvingar president Trump att förhandla med Demokraterna om finanspolitiken och utnämningar, exempelvis till Fed. Inom immigrations-, handels-och utrikespolitiken har presidenten stora frihetsgrader. De oväntat stora demokratiska framgångarna i mellanårsvalet pressar dock Republikanerna och väcker frågan om delar av partiet kan göra gemensam sak med Demokraterna kring kriget med Iran eller för Ukraina. Det lokala motståndet mot nya datacenter oroar börsen, men vi räknar inte med några stora förändringar inom vår prognoshorisont. 
FX Sales: Säkra höga USD/SEK-nivåer
Den amerikanska dollarn har legat på årshögstanivåer mot kronan sedan i september, men våra prognoser pekar mot en kommande försvagning. Utsikter till en lösning på konflikten i Mellanöstern och lägre energipriser bör i kombination med en fortsatt hög svensk tillväxt, starka svenska statsfinanser och ytterligare riksbankshöjning skapa förutsättningar för en återhämtning i kronan. Detta skapar en risk på nedsidan för företag med överskott av USD.

articles.title: High core CPI for a third month in a row
articles.heading: US inflation
articles.fulltext:
October CPI surprised on the upside with a 0.3% m/m increase, beating the consensus (0.2% m/m) for the second consecutive month. The surprise was relatively small but broad-based and the annualized 3-month change for core CPI is approaching 4%, while the year-on-year change is approaching 3%. Monthly data are volatile and year-on-year inflation has moved very little, but core inflation shows signs of accelerating slightly instead of slowing. The recent sharp decline in oil prices will, if sustained, exert downward pressure on headline inflation and with a lag also remove some of the upward pressure on core CPI.   
Key points
Core CPI 0.3%, 2.8% y/y, SEB 0.2%, 2.7% y/y, consensus 0.2%, previous 0.3%, 2.6%.
Headline CPI 0.4%, 4.0%, SEB 0.4%, 4.0% y/y, consensus 0.3% previous 0.6%, 3.7% y/y.
The upside surprise was small, but broadly based, and goods excluding used cars, services as well as rents were higher than expected.
Our preliminary estimate for core PCE is 0.33%
Since there are no indices for October 2025 (because of the government shut-down), there are no official estimates for the year-on-year inflation rates and the October numbers above are estimated by SEB.
Broadly based increases
Core CPI increased by 0.30% in October, above our (+0.25% m/m) and the consensus expectations for a slightly above 0.2% month-on-month increase. The year-on-year rate increased from 2.6% to 2.8%. The surprise was broadly based. Core services ex rents were increased by 0.4% and rents by (0.29%) were all 0.1-0.15 percentage points above our forecast. Core goods were 0.1pp lower than expected, but only because of lower prices on used cars while other goods were 0.1-0.5pp higher than expected at 0.4% m/m. Tourist services, which have been important drivers of higher inflation the last two months, continued to increase but at a more modest pace. 
Energy prices (0.7%) increased slightly less than expected and at a more modest pace compared to the last two months. Food prices increased by a higher than expected 0.4% m/m, after being muted three months in a row. 
Third consecutive disappointment 
The monthly price changes for the core CPI are still within the volatile range of the past two years. Monthly core CPI has tended to surprise on the downside this year but has been higher than expected during 3 months in a row. The 3-month annualized change is now at the high end of the recent range and approaching 4%. This will concern some members of the Fed, who often focuses on this measure. 
Short-term upside risks have increased
The renewed increase in energy prices has delayed the slowdown for headline inflation and has raised the risks for indirect effects from, for instance, higher transportation costs. Some signs of higher goods prices are emerging, and we have revised our near-term forecast slightly higher. There are also some signs that rents could start to rise at a slightly higher rate again, judging from the changes in market-based Zillow rents (see chart). This could reflect increased demand for rentals, driven by deteriorating affordability to purchase a home on the back of higher mortgage rates. Wage inflation continues to slow, however, which implies that any upturn in inflation will be temporary. The inflation outlook is significantly more uncertain than normal, but we continue to predict that underlying inflation trends will improve as temporary impulses from tariffs, energy prices and the AI build-out fade. Our forecast implies that both core CPI and core PCE will back at the target by the end of 2028.

articles.title: NOK 2bn in NST481 and NST485
articles.heading: NGB Spotlight
articles.fulltext:
On Wednesday Nov 11th, Norges Bank will hold a multiple tap auction where a total of NOK 2bn will be issued, split between the NST481 (1.75%, 09/2029) and the NST485 (3.50%, 10/2042) bonds. NST481 currently trades with a yield of 4.575%, implying a maturity-matched spread vs. Germany of 157.5bps and an ASW spread of -26.5bps. NST485 trades with a yield of 4.13%, with corresponding spread levels at 62bps and -4.75bps. The auction closes at 11.00 CET, and results will be available on Norges Bank’s website at 11.05 CET. Ahead of the auction there will be a buyback auction of NST479 (1.75%, 02/2027) which closes at 10:00 CET.
Details
On Wednesday, Norges Bank will auction a total of NOK 2bn split between NST481 (09/2029) and the NST485 (10/2042) bonds. The longer tenor has only been included in one auction so far this year and the bond received a bid-to-cover of 2.25 with an allotment share of 35%. NST 481, on the other hand, has been tapped 6 times so far this year, with an average bid-to-cover ratio of 4.0 and allotment share of 47%. We believe demand will be centered on NST481, and with the total volume capped at NOK 2bn we expect the auction to run smoothly.
In addition, there will be an ad hoc buyback auction of NST479 (02/2027). This is replacing the auction that was cancelled in conjunction with the 20y syndication. Outstanding amount before the action (incl. government’s own holdings) is NOK 54.975bn. 
Short yields have corrected sharply lower over the past week, reflecting falling oil prices and AI-related risk-off. This has not been reflected in NST479 resulting in a sharp inversion in the very front end of the yield curve. Hence, rolling into surrounding bonds from NST479 offers a negative yield pick-up.
 The auction closes at 10:00 CET, and announcement of auction result will be released at 10:05 CET.  
Norwegian bonds continue to trade directional with global trends. Long yields have fallen substantially over the past week, correcting much of the upturn after summer. Norwegian bonds have outperformed Germany in the rally, while underperforming marginally against swaps across the curve. The mid-segment of the ASW curve appears cheap after a long period with large selling pressures. Meanwhile, outright levels continue to attract demand from internationals.
Core inflation eased further to 2.7% y/y in 
October
 in line with Norges Bank’s projection. Market pricing corrected lower after the release and the market now discounts only a 20 percent probability for another rate hike (around year-end), and a full rate cut by March 2028. We reiterate our forecast that the hiking cycle has likely peaked, with policy easing not expected to begin before late 2027. Our inflation forecast is higher than Norges Bank’s near-term trajectory, but we predict slightly lower core inflation in 2027. 
Supply update: Following this auction, Norges Bank has issued a total of NOK 103bn YTD, while the annual borrowing interval is set at NOK 100-110bn (107-110bn in the Q4 guidance). We expect Norges Bank to issue the maximum amount, implying NOK 3bn in one of the 3 remaining auctions and NOK 2bn for the remaining auctions.
Supply 2027: The government’s budget proposal for 2027 showed an underlying borrowing requirement of NOK 93.6bn vs. 95.7bn in 2026. After years of under-borrowing, Norges Bank’s supply estimate has exceeded the underlying borrowing requirement over the past two years, with the aim of building up the cash reserves. We expect this to be the case also in 2027, implying a minimum of NOK 110bn in gross supply. The government’s borrowing mandate in long-term debt is increased by NOK 50bn to NOK 200bn, to provide greater flexibility and allowing for a potential increase in its own holdings. Risks to our supply estimate are thus skewed to the upside. Details will be provided in Norges Bank’s Strategy and borrowing programme due in December.

articles.title: Small changes to nominal bond issuance
articles.heading: The SNDO borrowing report
articles.fulltext:
We predict the National Debt Office (NDO) to make minor changes to nominal bond issuance and reduce the number of planned auctions in 2027 to 45 from currently planned 48 (total issuance will be reduced to SEK 225bn from SEK 240bn in 2027) in the November 26 Central government borrowing report. The outlook for the borrowing is, however, a bit more uncertain than normal.
The outlook for the budget balance: 
The budget balance has been SEK 40bn higher than the Debt Office’s forecast since May, but almost all deviation is explained by a pre-payment of SEK 38bn for fighter jets. These are planned to be delivered to Ukraine in 2029-2030, and our understanding is that the pre-payment will remain at the Debt Office until then. This will lower debt issuance in the near term but is a one-off, expected to be gradually reversed over the next 3-4 years. Excluding this, the budget balance has been close to the NDO’s forecast. Both tax revenues and expenditure have been largely as expected. 
Stronger growth: 
The NDO is likely to revise the 2026 GDP growth upwards by around 1 percentage point to 2.9%. This is expected to motivate an upward revision of the budget balance projection by SEK 10bn in 2026 and SEK 20bn in 2027. Growth impacts on government finances are uncertain, and employment, which is important for tax revenues, has been developing largely in line with the NDO’s forecast.
Pre-payment from EU:
 A one-off payment from the EU (NextGeneration) will lift the budget balance in 2026 by about SEK 40bn.
Re-lending to the Riksbank:
 The Riksbank plans to fund parts of the currency reserve by taking up FX loans via the NDO. If decided, which is highly likely, the Riksbank will request the NDO to borrow foreign currency amounting to SEK 200bn for re-lending. We expect the NDO to wait for a formal request before including the measure in the forecast, but the final impact on the budget balance will likely be a decrease of SEK 135bn in 2027 and SEK 65bn in 2028.
Fiscal policy: 
In the May borrowing report, the NDO assumed SEK 15bn in unfinanced fiscal policy. We think there is some scope for an upwards revision, but we predict that the first budget from a new government will be cautious. If no new government is in place before the 12 Nov (which seems unlikely), the caretaker government will present a caretaker budget, which by praxis should be neutral and stripped-down. However, 27 Nov is the final deadline for parties/coalitions to submit their own budget propositions.
Defence and support to Ukraine: 
The government is gradually raising defence spending and has announced a scope for military support to Ukraine amounting to slightly less than 1% of GDP per year in 2026 and 2027. It is difficult to follow actual developments in real time, but our view is that both support to Ukraine and national military spending has been delayed.
Despite revising the budget balance upwards in 2026 and 2027, 
we predict nominal bond issuance to be lowered by SEK 15bn to SEK 225bn in 2027, most likely by reducing the number of auctions to 45 from 48.
The NDO changes nominal bond supply only gradually, and temporary deviations to the expected budget balance will primarily affect T-bills and other short-term funding. In addition, T-bill funding is currently high as share of outstanding debt. 
Even if the budget deficit is expected to improve eventually, a large chunk of bonds is maturing in 2028, and bond issuance will probably need to stay above SEK 200bn. The NDO is gradually replacing a large share of maturing inflation-linked bonds by nominal bonds.
When the re-lending to the Riksbank starts in 2027, the NDO will most likely revise the previously planned FX-bond issuance to zero. Despite that the NDO will not include the re-lending in their November forecast, this could on the margin affect issuance plans already for 2027. Issuance previously planned in FX bonds may be re-directed to SGBs, which could lower the downside pressure on SGB issuance.

articles.title: Financial Forecasts 10 November
articles.heading: Financial Forecasts
articles.fulltext:
This is a snapshot of our forecasts. You will always find our latest forecasts and published analysis and comments at

articles.title: Minutes more hawkish than the policy statement
articles.heading: Riksbank minutes in detail
articles.fulltext:
The minutes are more hawkish than the press statement and Policy Update last week, mainly due to Per Jansson and Göran Hjelm.
 Jansson and Hjelm both highlighted upside risks to inflation due to high energy prices and stronger economic activity, with Jansson worrying over the persistence of elevated oil and gas prices and Hjelm referring to the large increase in producer prices. Hjelm has been the most dovish member of the Board since his start, tending to reason more from a real-economy perspective.
In contrast, Anna Seim, who we had expected to argue for more aggressive rate hikes, refers to the September rate path without any explicit mentions about the timing or size of further tightening. However, she seems to keep the door open for a rate hike in December, which is unsurprising given previous communication. More unexpectedly, so did Per Jansson, who said that a rate hike in November did not rule out another hike in December. Nonetheless, Jansson seems to see this as a risk, not a main scenario.
Governor Erik Thedéen sounded balanced, having previously leaned more hawkishly. He says that he expects the policy rate to be raised in line with the September forecast over the coming six months or so. Indicating a rate hike is slightly more hawkish than “in the coming year”, which was the wording in the press release. Thedéen doe, however, not seem to consider hiking rates in September. Bunge remained in the more dovish camp, with risks highlighted in both directions, underscoring the need for a gradual approach. However, she agrees with the rest of the Board saying that the direction higher in rates is clear.
Policy conclusion:
 Overall, Board members refer to the gradual tightening set out in their forecast as a normalisation as the economic recovery gains grounds amidst high energy prices. Our impression is more hawkish than expected given last week's decision, especially given Jansson and Hjelm's reasoning. At the same time, it is worth pointing out that Board members, to some extent, are putting forward their arguments for hiking - not necessarily for further rate hikes in the near-term.
In our opinion, the low inflation print in October, coupled with a general re-pricing of central banks, a stronger SEK and lower energy prices, all point to an unchanged rate in December. We expect the Riksbank to raise the policy rate in March and maintain it at 2.25 per cent until the end of 2028. Stronger growth implies that there are upside risks to our forecast.
As per usual, we have ranked the individual Board members on our dove-hawk scale. See more details on each individual member below.
Bunge (1): 
Signs of changed pricing behaviour could strengthen the need for a tighter monetary policy and require swifter action from us. If household demand becomes weaker than expected, companies’ possibilities to raise their prices will also decline, and this can reduce the need to continue tightening monetary policy. We should apply a gradual approach going forward. The Swedish economy is moving towards a normal economic situation, which also suggests that monetary policy should be normalised. Important to consider that the strength of the recovery could be tested if we proceed too quickly with rate increases. We should carefully evaluate the need for each step going forward. That said, the direction is clear, and a tighter monetary policy will likely be needed going forward to keep inflation at the target.
Hjelm (2)
: I assess that upside risks dominate relative to the inflation forecasts from September. I assess the current level of the policy rate to be mildly expansionary. The economic recovery has become clearer. Most importantly for my assessment at this meeting, is that the supply disruptions and the cost increases they entail have become larger and lasted longer than previously feared. It remains to be seen to what extent the policy rate needs to be raised to achieve this overall, but I assess a further increase as likely given the current outlook.
If, in a parallel universe, we had had the same forecast picture for inflation and resource utilisation but without the cost-driving supply disruptions and the risk profile they entail, the option value of waiting further with a rate hike would have outweighed other factors. It would then have been appropriate to await even clearer signs that the idle resources in the labour market would be utilised before the policy rate needed to be raised. However, we are now here, and therefore I support the draft Monetary Policy Update.
Thedéen (3): 
Important to focus on the measures of underlying inflation that provide the best guidance as to how consumer prices will develop over time (CPIF excluding energy and effects of temporary fiscal policy measures). Sees a significant risk that continued supply related cost increases, linked to the geopolitical situation globally, will interact with an increasingly strong economy. In such a scenario, it is entirely possible that the policy rate would need to be raised a few times more. In a scenario with weaker growth compared to the assumption in the main scenario, and with a slower increase in underlying inflation, the policy rate would likely not need to be raised to the extent indicated in our latest forecast. I view the policy rate forecast from September as a weighting of a few such different scenarios. The main scenario implies a probable continued normalisation of monetary policy. I expect that we will raise the policy rate in line with our September forecast over the coming six months or so.
Seim (4): 
Seim highlights the declining consumer sentiment and that this is a downside risk to growth. However, Seim seems more concerned over the impact on households from high inflation concluding that acting early reduces the risk that we will need to act more forcefully later. Furthermore, the September policy-rate path should be seen as a normalisation of monetary policy, not as a dramatic tightening. “We will publish new forecasts in December and, as always, remain fully prepared to adjust monetary policy should this prove warranted”. The final remark could indicate that Seim is open to a rate hike in December, although other comments about the rate path are in line with the September rate path.  
Jansson (5): 
Jansson highlights lower-than-expected September inflation, but also the strong upward pressure on inflation from energy prices and that headline inflation would be well above the target. Jansson concludes that the inflation picture has “become more complicated since our meeting in September” and that “it is appropriate to act at today’s meeting rather than wait any longer”. According to Jansson, a price wage spiral in line with the 1970s and 1980s would be very costly to break. Raising the policy rate now does not rule out the possibility of also needing to raise it at in December. The September forecast relates to the total number of increases envisaged in September – namely just under two further increases, rather than the exact timing. I still have high hopes that the increases in our current monetary policy plan will be sufficient to eventually stabilise inflation around the target.
